source_term: batch formation waiting / waiting queue before batch processing
formula: sum_b sum_{o in members(b)} max(0, batch_start_b - operation_ready_o)
project_canonical_formula: sum_b sum_{o in members(b)} max(0, batch_start_b - operation_ready_o)
objective_path: batch formation and start decision -> operations wait for compatible batch members/capacity -> delayed downstream completion -> makespan
applicability: parallel or family batch-processing machines with explicit batch membership and readiness times
counterexample_boundary: can increase when fuller batches reduce later machine cycles; may be off the critical path
degenerate_when: every batch has one member or starts when each member becomes ready
missing_data_behavior: semantic_only; do not infer from completion times alone

source_locators.supporting_passage_summary: Operations assigned to a parallel batch share start/end times and are placed in a waiting queue before batch allocation; the paper does not define this project metric formula.

source_term: unused batch capacity / batch fill loss
formula: sum_b max(0, capacity_b - load_b) / sum_b capacity_b
project_canonical_formula: sum_b max(0, capacity_b - load_b) / sum_b capacity_b
objective_path: batch composition/sequence -> unused capacity and number of batch cycles -> machine completion span -> makespan
applicability: capacity-constrained batch processors or blocking devices with explicit slot/capacity semantics
counterexample_boundary: forcing fuller batches may create long formation waits and worsen makespan
degenerate_when: all batches have unit capacity or capacity is never binding
missing_data_behavior: return null; batch count is not a substitute for capacity

source_locators.supporting_passage_summary: Defines unused packaging slots as blocking loss; general batch-capacity normalization here is project-defined.

formula: sum_g sum_{l in sublots(g)} max(0, downstream_start_g - sublot_ready_{g,l})
project_canonical_formula: sum_g sum_{l in sublots(g)} max(0, downstream_start_g - sublot_ready_{g,l})
objective_path: lot split and sublot sequence -> unequal sublot arrivals at merge/assembly -> synchronization waiting -> makespan
applicability: lot streaming/splitting with explicit parent lot and downstream merge or joint-completion gate
counterexample_boundary: not applicable when sublots remain independent; smaller sublots may reduce makespan despite higher aggregate early-sublot waiting
degenerate_when: no lot is split or all sublots reach the merge simultaneously
missing_data_behavior: not_applicable unless an explicit merge/joint gate exists

source_locators.supporting_passage_summary: Distinguishes lot streaming from independent lot splitting and studies setup interactions; no metric formula was available from the abstract.

source_term: WIP level / work-in-process inventory over time
objective_path: job release/sequence -> WIP congestion and queueing -> resource starvation/blocking interactions -> makespan
applicability: requires release/completion or WIP event trace; especially informative in reentrant or finite-buffer systems
counterexample_boundary: lower WIP can starve bottlenecks and increase makespan; when all jobs release at zero it is closely related to total flow time
degenerate_when: single job or fixed release/completion profile across candidates
missing_data_behavior: partial_metric only if release and completion times are complete

source_locators.supporting_passage_summary: Uses WIP control to manage waiting in a reentrant hybrid flow shop; the integral metric is project-defined.

source_term: reentrant visit waiting / revisit queue delay
formula: sum_{visit v with index>1} max(0, start_v - revisit_ready_v)
project_canonical_formula: sum_{visit v with index>1} max(0, start_v - revisit_ready_v)
objective_path: release and revisit sequencing -> repeated-stage queues -> delayed later layers -> makespan
applicability: routes revisit a machine or stage and each visit has a stable visit index
counterexample_boundary: may be displaced to first-visit queues or off-critical jobs; not defined for ordinary acyclic routes
degenerate_when: no route revisits any stage or repeated visits start immediately

source_locators.supporting_passage_summary: Models repeated workstation visits and stockers; the revisit-specific waiting formula is project-defined.

objective_path: worker assignment and route -> transfer occupation/late arrival -> operation readiness delay -> makespan
applicability: workers move between locations and transfer duration is not included in processing time
counterexample_boundary: transfer can occur while no assigned operation is ready; total transfer time may change without affecting makespan
degenerate_when: workers are station-fixed or all locations have zero transfer time
missing_data_behavior: do not infer from gaps in worker utilization

source_locators.supporting_passage_summary: Explicitly studies worker transfer delays and identifies worker utilization as an underlying variable; no exact metric formula was available.

canonical_name: 人员工作负荷变异系数
objective_path: worker assignment -> worker bottleneck/imbalance -> synchronized machine delays -> makespan
applicability: heterogeneous workers with assignments and available-time calendars
counterexample_boundary: balancing non-bottleneck workers can worsen machine assignments; zero mean utilization makes CV undefined
degenerate_when: one worker or fixed worker assignment
missing_data_behavior: return null when available capacity or worker identity is missing

source_locators.section: worker multi-functionality and efficiency matrices; simulation outcomes
source_locators.supporting_passage_summary: Shows heterogeneous worker eligibility and efficiency materially affect lead time and other performance; CV normalization is project-defined.

source_term: fixture loading and unloading setup time
formula: sum_o setup_time_o, where setup_time_o is the triggered fixture loading plus unloading time
source_formula: T = sum_i sum_j sd_ij; sd_ij is defined from fixture loading s_fm and unloading d_fm in Eq. (3)
objective_path: fixture assignment and machine sequence -> fixture load/unload setup -> operation start delays -> makespan
applicability: operations require assignable fixtures/tools with explicit loading and unloading times
counterexample_boundary: reducing fixture changes may select slower machines or overload a fixture bottleneck
degenerate_when: fixtures are permanently mounted or all loading/unloading times are zero
missing_data_behavior: do not collapse generic setup time into this decomposition unless fixture semantics are explicit

source_locators.section: The model of DRFJSP-LU; Notations; Formulation
source_locators.supporting_passage_summary: Defines total setup time T as the sum of operation setup times and decomposes each setup into fixture loading and unloading contributions.

canonical_name: AGV 充电导致的任务等待
objective_path: vehicle assignment and charging schedule -> vehicle unavailable at transport request -> material delivery delay -> machine starvation/makespan
applicability: battery-constrained AGVs with charge intervals and transport request/dispatch timestamps
counterexample_boundary: planned charging during naturally idle periods can increase total charging time without increasing task waiting
degenerate_when: battery constraints never bind or charging occurs outside all pending task intervals
missing_data_behavior: semantic_only without charge-attribution or battery trace

source_locators.supporting_passage_summary: Jointly schedules AGV assignment, sequencing and flexible charging; the charging-attributed waiting formula is project-defined.

formula: sum_a sum_{c in components(a)} max(0, assembly_start_a - component_delivered_time_c)
project_canonical_formula: sum_a sum_{c in components(a)} max(0, assembly_start_a - component_delivered_time_c)
objective_path: processing/transport/assembly decisions -> unequal component arrivals -> early-component waiting and assembly start delay -> makespan
applicability: assembly task requires multiple completed/delivered components
counterexample_boundary: early arrival may be intentionally buffered; aggregate component waiting can rise while assembly critical path shortens
degenerate_when: each assembly has one component or all components arrive simultaneously

source_locators.section: processing–transportation–assembly problem description and MILP model
source_locators.supporting_passage_summary: Models jobs processed, transported by AGVs and assembled downstream; component-level waiting aggregation is project-defined.

formula: sum_s weight_s * indicator(schedule infeasible in scenario s) / sum_s weight_s
project_canonical_formula: sum_s weight_s * indicator(schedule infeasible in scenario s) / sum_s weight_s
objective_path: baseline decisions -> scenario-specific constraint violations -> executable-schedule failure; this is primarily a robustness diagnostic, not a deterministic makespan mediator
applicability: scenario set contains hard-constraint validation outcomes and weights or a declared equal-weight sampling rule
counterexample_boundary: if recourse always repairs feasibility, the metric becomes zero and hides repair cost/delay
degenerate_when: single deterministic scenario or validator marks every scenario feasible by construction
missing_data_behavior: diagnostic_unknown; do not treat solver failure as schedule infeasibility

source_locators.supporting_passage_summary: Distinguishes solution robustness, performance robustness and stability; the infeasibility-rate diagnostic is project-defined.

objective_path: rescheduling policy -> number of schedule revisions and operational nervousness; not necessarily a makespan mediator
applicability: dynamic experiment records baseline publication and each rescheduling epoch
counterexample_boundary: fewer rescheduling events can allow disruptions to accumulate and worsen makespan; periodic policies may fix the count externally
degenerate_when: one-shot scheduling or a policy with fixed number of epochs
missing_data_behavior: return null; schedule version count is not equivalent unless version semantics are audited

source_locators.supporting_passage_summary: Discusses dynamic events and trade-offs between efficiency, robustness and stability; event count remains a project-defined policy measure.
